levels.description: Use booleans and if/else to choose a route.
levels.objective: The if/else route is ready. Change the lit-path step count so you reach the gate at (7, 2).
levels.starter_code:

if lantern_lit:

hero.move_right(steps)

steps = [1, 1, 1, 1, 1]
total = 0
for step in steps:

levels.starter_code:

def double_steps(steps):
    pass  # Return twice the number of steps.

hero.move_right(double_steps(2) + 1)

levels.description: Combine Python basics to open the gate without RGB spells.
levels.objective: Follow the short path to collect the key and fill the Lock Flask. At the gate, finish the opening f-string with Eldrin's name.

hero.pick_up()

levels.description: Learn for loops to iterate over lists.
levels.objective: Brighten every channel by 30, stopping at 255. A for loop applies the same image filter to every pixel. Complete the marked line; the casting path is ready.
levels.starter_code:
def transform(pixels):
    result = []
    for pixel in pixels:
        result.append(pixel)  # Add 30 to each channel, capped at 255.
    return result

pixels = [[50,70,90],[140,40,70],[240,220,200]]
colors = transform(pixels)
for index, color in enumerate(colors):
    hero.cast_color(color[0], color[1], color[2])
    if index < 2:
        # Walk around the rock, then return to the rune row.
        hero.move_up(1)
        hero.move_right(3)
        hero.move_down(1)

levels.description: Repair a broken pixel processing loop.
levels.objective: Fix the loop so it adds 20 to red only, capped at 255; keep green and blue. A faulty loop shifts pixel channels and corrupts an image. Complete the marked line; the casting path is ready.
levels.starter_code:
def transform(pixels):
    result = []
    for pixel in pixels:
        result.append([min(255, pixel[1] + 20), pixel[0], pixel[2]])
    return result

pixels = [[20,40,90],[80,140,30],[250,20,50]]
colors = transform(pixels)
for index, color in enumerate(colors):
    hero.cast_color(color[0], color[1], color[2])
    if index < 2:
        # Walk around the rock, then return to the rune row.
        hero.move_up(1)
        hero.move_right(3)
        hero.move_down(1)

levels.description: Use a simple loop to turn red cave runes gold.
levels.objective: Turn pixels with red above 100 gold. Keep the others unchanged. A loop can spot red cave runes and recolor them one by one. Complete the marked line; the casting path is ready.
levels.starter_code:
def transform(pixels):
    result = []
    for pixel in pixels:
        if False:  # Is the red channel above 100?
            result.append([255, 200, 40])
        else:
            result.append(pixel)
    return result

pixels = [[30,40,50],[200,30,20],[70,80,90]]
colors = transform(pixels)
for index, color in enumerate(colors):
    hero.cast_color(color[0], color[1], color[2])
    if index < 2:
        # Walk around the rock, then return to the rune row.
        hero.move_up(1)
        hero.move_right(3)
        hero.move_down(1)
hero.move_right(2)
hero.move_down(2)

levels.objective: Make pixels white when red is at least 128; otherwise make them black. A simple color check can reveal bright red pixels.

levels.objective: Use red below 85 for blue, below 170 for gold, and otherwise white. if/elif/else can choose a color from the red value.

levels.description: Combine boolean masks to reveal hidden pixels.
levels.objective: Keep pixels with red above 100; make the others black. A color check can hide pixels that are not red enough.

levels.description: Turn dark pixels gold with a simple color choice.
levels.objective: Turn pixels whose red is below 100 gold. Keep the others unchanged. A red-channel check can reveal the dark parts of an image. Complete the marked line; the casting path is ready.
levels.starter_code:
def transform(pixels):
    result = []
    for r, g, b in pixels:
        if False:  # Is red below 100?
            result.append([255, 200, 40])
        else:
            result.append([r, g, b])
    return result

pixels = [[20,30,40],[180,60,40],[40,150,240]]
colors = transform(pixels)
for index, color in enumerate(colors):
    hero.cast_color(color[0], color[1], color[2])
    if index < 2:
        # Walk around the rock, then return to the rune row.
        hero.move_up(1)
        hero.move_right(3)
        hero.move_down(1)
